chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Abi Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Sukayn ibn 'Ammar, from a man among our companions who was known by the kunyah Abu Ahmad, who said:

I was with Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام in the tawaf, and his hand was in my hands, or my hands were in his hand, when a man with a need came to me. So I gestured to him with my hand and said to him: Stay as you are until I finish my tawaf. Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said during the tawaf: What is this? I said: May Allah set you aright, a man came to me with a need. He said to me: Is he a Muslim? I said: Yes. He said: Go with him concerning his need. I said to him: May Allah set you aright, and should I cut off the tawaf? He said: Yes. I said: Even if it is the obligatory one? He said: Yes, even if you are in the obligatory one.

He said: And Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Whoever walks with his Muslim brother regarding a need, Allah writes for him one million good deeds, erases from him one million evil deeds, and raises for him one million degrees.

key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the circumambulation around the Ka'bah performed as an act of worship
key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضِ: that which is obligatory, here referring to obligatory tawaf
key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: a need or matter requiring assistance
key_terms.حَسَنَةٍ: a good deed recorded as reward
key_terms.دَرَجَةٍ: a rank or degree elevated by Allah
key_terms.سَيِّئَةٍ: an evil deed or sin that is erased

ai.seo_question: Can a person interrupt tawaf, even an obligatory tawaf, to help a Muslim in need?
ai.summary: This hadith states that assisting a Muslim brother in his need may take precedence even over continuing tawaf, including obligatory tawaf. It also emphasizes the immense reward Allah grants for accompanying and helping a fellow Muslim in fulfilling his need.
